To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P2X receptors of various subtypes are expressed in identified RGCs.
P2X receptor mRNA is expressed in retinal ganglionic cells and that the P2X(4) receptor is expressed in the retina.
P2X receptors (P2X3-P2X5) are expressed in RGCs of the adult rat and that extracellular ATP may provide neuromodalulatory influences on information-processing in the retina.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of purinergic receptor expression patterns in RGCs of the adult rat.
the identification and localization of P2X receptor expression in retinal ganglionic cells (RGC).
the molecular characterization of the P2X(2-5) and P2X(1) receptor subtypes in RGCs and the functional role of these receptors in the retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATP is an important neurotransmitter in the retina.
P2X receptors, especially P2X(4) and P2X(5), are present in the retina and that these receptors may be involved in the processing of visual information.
P2X receptors may play a role in retinal physiology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP is an important neurotransmitter for the retina.
the retina expresses P2X receptor channels and these channels may be involved in the modulation of synaptic transmission in the inner retina.
P2X receptors play an important role in the regulation of the retinal function and may be involved in the development of retinal degenerative diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P2X receptors may be a novel target for the development of new drugs to prevent or treat retinal diseases.
the P2X(4) receptor is the most abundant subtype in RGCs, and that the P2XR(3) receptor is the least abundant subtype.
the P2X receptor family is expressed in a variety of cells in the eye.
